Zuckerberg Says AI Labs Should Handle Safety Risks Themselves
"Every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens," Zuckerberg wrote on
He argued that AI companies already have strong reasons to prioritize safety.
Users, he said, will avoid AI agents that fail to follow their instructions or act against their interests, making alignment an increasingly important competitive factor.
"There is a lot of debate about slowing progress on capabilities until alignment catches up. My view is that … any lab that doesn’t focus on alignment will fall behind."
Zuckerberg also said labs face “significant liability” if their models cause harm, giving them a strong incentive to prevent such risks.
Meta Delayed Muse Over Safety Concerns
The Meta CEO then pointed to Meta’s Muse as an example of the company taking action on its own. He said Meta delayed the agent’s launch for months while it focused on safety and security.
"We didn’t call for everyone else to do this before we would," Zuckerberg said. "We just did it as part of our day-to-day work because it was clearly the right thing for people and for us."
He also advocated for greater use of independent evaluators and advisers to test AI systems, saying a broader and more diverse ecosystem of evaluators would benefit the industry.
